newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Southern sees continued dividend growth.
newsitem.headline: Southern sees continued dividend growth.

text.p: South African life assurer and financial services company, Southern Life Association Ltd, said on Wednesday that shareholders can expect continued real growth in dividends.

The group said in a statement accompanying its end of year results that strategic transformation projects currently underway in the firm and in the asset management unit will enhance operation and financial efficiency.
"(This will also)...reposition both companies to meet the challenges of the changing financial services markets," Southern said.

It said that the increase in the share price of First National Bank Holdings, in which Southern owns a 24 percent stake, together with the overall improvement in the Johannesburg Stock Exchange had provided a boost for Southern.
"(This) has resulted in the excess of assets over actuarial liabilities regaining much of the ground lost during 1996/97," Southern said.
Southern earlier reported earnings per share for the year ended March 31 rising to 267.0 cents a share from 216.0 before. It raised its dividend to 178.0 cents from 144.0 a year ago.
